questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a university which was not in a big city and which also had a good academic programme. It was definitely a plus that University of Limerick was in an English-speaking country, and that it was not very far from Copenhagen either.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of information given to us by the UL Erasmus team as well as from the UCPH coordinators, so I would say we had all the necessary information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The UL Erasmus team had planned a whole orientation week just for international students when we arrived, so we could get to know each other, the university and a bit of Ireland as well, which was really thoughtful. They gave us social and academic support and overall were very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You were able to get a room in a shared apartment.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: All apartments have kitchens, but there are no meal plans available.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Remember to apply for student accommodation as soon as possible, and be prepared for not getting it. We were six people from UCPH going to UL, and only three of us were granted on-campus accommodation, which left the remaining three students in quite an unlucky situation. There is a housing crisis in all of Ireland which of course effects UL and Limerick, so it is very difficult to find accommodation - and even if you find available accommodation it will probably be expensive, far away from campus and in spaces without a lot of privacy. UL are able to host MOST international students, but just be aware that there is a chance that you might have to look for accommodation on your own.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was happy with the student accommodation, but I was not happy with the fact that not all of us from UCPH were able to get it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was a bit confusing, because we had to registrate several times on different platforms. When our semester begun, we had a "trial period" of about 4 weeks, where we could try out different courses before deciding on which ones to follow. This was very nice, as you were able to meet the professor, check out the course plan and exam form before enrolling in the course, but it of course dragged out the process quite a lot.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of help available from the Erasmus team and all the professors were very helpful with answering questions both in class and via email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There was no limit on the amount of international students who could enroll in courses, so you were able to choose whichever course you wanted, which was really nice.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not stress about it before going, just show up at UL, see which courses are available and try out as many as possible before deciding.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The theoretical level was definitely lower than what I am used to at UCPH, and there was almost no required reading in my courses. Instead we had to write a lot of essays where we had to research literature and structure assignments ourselves, which we were not used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Almost all of my courses consisted of one or two weekly lectures and a weekly tutorial, all in smaller classes of about 20-40 students, so it was a lot more personal that the lectures I am used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) Comparative European Politics
2) Policy-making in the European Union
3) Russian Politics
4) Government and Politics in Ireland
5) Nationality, Ethnicity and Conflict

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend them all except Government and Politics in Ireland - the course focuses a lot on Irish political history and Irish bureaucracy, and it is quite difficult to keep up with that level of detail when you are not Irish.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There were not any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Almost everything costs the same as in Denmark - grocery stores and restaurants are a bit cheaper, but not a lot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were so many clubs and societies, almost anything you could imagine - there were clubs for kayaking, fencing, photography, soccer, climbing, running, sailing, dancing, yoga, reading and fashion, just to name a few.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would especially recommend kayaking and surfing. There are sessions every week so you are able to keep up with the club and really get to know the other members, and they plan a lot of weekend trips which are so much fun. But generally are all the clubs very nice, so I would recommend just trying a bunch of different ones.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Definitely travel around Ireland and go on hiking trips. I would recommend Connomara, Galway, Dingle, Killarney and Wicklow. Dublin is also not far away and the bus goes all night, so definitely spend some Saturdays in Dublin once in a while - you can really do a lot in a day.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy - Irish culture is very open and not too different from Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences really challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated the openness towards international students, as it is not that common in Denmark. Also the pub culture in Ireland is just really great and chill!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Join clubs! Most courses you will take will mostly be with international students, so being in the clubs are a great way to meet and befriend Irish students
2) If you live on campus, remember to go into Limerick city and use its cafés to study and pubs to party. I would especially recommend Canteen and Nancy Blakes
3) Start your exams early. I mostly had to turn in essays which I had all semester to do, but I ended up having to do most of them in a hurry at the end of the semester, which was a shame - at the end of the semester you want to enjoy the place and your friends while you can, so you don't want to be stressing over exams by then.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get an Irish phone number quick so you can order groceries from Dunnes and Tesco.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
It was really rewarding getting a lot of new great friends, both Danish, Swedish, Australian, German and Irish (and more). All international students are away from home and their usual friends so everyone are very open to meet new people, so it was quite easy to get new friends and get close to them fast. 

It was also very rewarding just trying to live in another country, and Ireland really is a great place. I felt very lucky to experience their lovely culture and amazing nature, and I can't wait to come back to visit - it definitely already feels like a home away from home.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Moving to a different country is generally challenging, just because you need to learn many things from scratch - where to grocery shop, how to take the bus, etc. I had never been to Ireland before coming to Limerick, so it was a bit overwhelming in the beginning, but there are so many international students in the same situation, so you will figure it out together.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
